finding.claim: deleteAccount performs no authorization check. canDelete(u, a) is called but its boolean result is discarded, so any caller who can reach DELETE /accounts/{id} can delete any account.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled id path parameter and the User u the caller is authenticated as (line 20). Precondition: any authenticated non-admin user, or any caller if the route lacks authentication.
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at src/AccountService.java:23, a destructive delete of another user's account.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) accepts an arbitrary id and user.
a = accounts.get(id) loads the target account, which may be owned by someone else.
canDelete(u, a) returns false for a non-owner non-admin, but the result is ignored. No throw, no early return.

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is logically correct: admin OR owner. The bug is that deleteAccount never acts on it. The guard that does throw, assertCanDelete (lines 13-17), is used only by closeAccount (line 29), so the DELETE path lacks it. Null handling: if the id is missing, a is null. For non-admins, a.ownerId() at line 10 throws NullPointerException, a 500 and not a bypass. For admins, the call succeeds and remove is a no-op. Neither grants access. Not verifiable from this repo: authentication of u, route-level middleware, and whether an outer layer checks ownership before deleteAccount is called.

verdict.guard_found: Only guard in the file is canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11), which returns a boolean. Its result is discarded by the bare call at line 22, so it has no effect. assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) would throw, but deleteAccount never calls it; it is used only by closeAccount (line 29). No route, middleware, or caller-side ownership check exists in the repo (only AccountService.java is present).
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the boolean from canDelete(u, a) is discarded, so deleteAccount reaches accounts.remove(id) at line 23 for any caller u, including a non-owner non-admin; the throwing guard assertCanDelete (line 13-17) is not used on this path. The trace lines all match the candidate. Caveat: the route that exposes DELETE /accounts/{id} is not in this repo, so whether an authenticated low-privilege user can reach it is assumed, not verified.
